checks: For any V⊆P, projection gives the reverse graph-hull implication and Jensen preservation with the same coefficients gives the forward implication. Apply it to every deletion of W. The lifted deletion hulls have empty common trace precisely when every base in P∩K(W) has nonintegral height. Every proper subfamily missing the deletion at w contains the lift of w, since all heights on W are integral. A singleton W has an empty deletion hull, so its condition is vacuous as required.

Each anchored coefficient polytope is a compact rational polytope, including the trivial representation when needed. Taking its vertices gives finitely many rational linear constraints and a rational function-space basis. Clearing denominators in the individual basis functions preserves the rational span and gives the integer row features.

A rational coefficient vector α defines a rational linear functional on Λ. Integrality on W makes its residue character trivial on Λ_W, and a common denominator of α bounds the order of its image. Conversely a ℤ-basis of the subgroup Λ⊆ℤ^ℓ is linearly independent over ℚ. Choose rational lifts of the character values on this basis, extend the resulting ℚ-linear functional to ℚ^ℓ, and reduce modulo integers to recover the original character on every row.

Every kernel base is in conv(W) and has a rational anchored representation from W. Every feature column preserves it, so a positive integer multiple of A_p lies in Λ_W and [A_p] is torsion. The torsion subgroup of the finitely generated quotient is finite. Its characters extend by zero on a free summand. The proof tests one character against all classes and does not replace simultaneous nonvanishing by separate nonzero tests.

Original 11867665f48c887c §§1–2 gives the same deletion-kernel transfer and character criterion. Its optional separation argument for hypothetical nontorsion classes is unnecessary for the actual deletion kernel. Its integer-trace conclusion follows from lattice completeness and the same graph-hull equivalence and is separately dispositioned.

dependencies.mapping: Use its canonical lift on the nonempty finite base P, with a basis of all real functions preserving anchored convex representations. A rational Jensen g belongs to that space, so its value is an affine restriction on the lift. The same convex coefficients preserve that value, and the affine projection recovers each original base, giving the exact deletion-hull membership equivalence.

overlap.comparison: The complete canonical lift preserves the anchored representations and hence the deletion-hull traces used here. It does not impose the integrality of one recovered scalar function or characterize which kernel classes can all be excluded.

The accepted construction clears denominators to make the added coordinates integral at every base and proves congruence preservation on that full lift. The frozen criterion instead varies a rational Jensen height and filters out particular sites, by testing characters on a quotient generated by a proposed W.

The finite-set witness lemma and the midpoint-closed graph Helly bound concern actual geometric traces. They do not characterize arithmetic feasibility of deleting all members of a specified kernel under a single rational height.

readability: Here a Helly witness is the critical family of deletion hulls of its lifted points. The proof makes the intended condition clear through the common deletion kernel.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The criterion correctly reduces a specified graph deletion witness to one simultaneous character test on a finite torsion subgroup.
